The teponaztli is a slit drum used by the Aztecs and related cultures of central Mexico; it is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.2. It is made from a hollowed hardwood log with an H-shaped double slit cut in the top face to form two tongues, struck with a rubber-headed mallet or a deer antler; because the tongues differ in length or thickness it can produce two pitches. The body may carry relief carving, and sizes run from about 30 cm to 1.2 m; larger ones stand on supports, and smaller ones can rest on a stand or be carried on a shoulder strap. Performance contexts include dance, poetry, celebration and war communication, and it often plays together with the huehuetl skin drum.
在阿茲特克帝國時期，特波那茲特鼓廣泛應用於宗教儀式、戰爭和慶典活動中。其深沉而富: In the period of the Aztec empire the teponaztli was widely used in religious ritual, war and celebration. Its deep, penetrating tone was held to have sacred meaning, and it was often used together with other percussion. The instrument's name comes from Nahuatl, which reflects its important place in ancient Mesoamerican culture.

特波那茲特鼓屬裂縫鼓，發聲來自空心硬木原木上切出的「H」形雙舌。兩舌因長短或厚薄: The teponaztli is a slit drum; its sound comes from the two H-shaped tongues cut into a hollow hardwood log. Because the tongues differ in length or thickness they produce two pitches, usually about a third or a fourth apart, so the range is narrow and the instrument mainly supplies rhythm and the contrast of two notes. The player strikes the tongues with a rubber-headed wooden mallet or a deer antler, and the sound comes from the vibration of the wooden tongues and the resonance of the cavity. Some drums are carved as an open-mouthed animal, with an opening at the end that increases the volume; others have a hole in the base. Large drums stand on supports, small ones can be carried on the shoulder, which suits dance, poetry recitation or war communication. Unlike a skin drum it does not rely on a drumhead but produces two notes from fixed wooden tongues.
特波那茲特鼓是墨西哥中部阿茲特克等文化的體鳴裂縫鼓。較大鼓置於支撐架，較小鼓可置: Larger drums stand on a support, smaller ones can rest on a stand or hang from a shoulder strap. To sound it, strike the tongues cut by the two slits in the top face with a rubber-headed mallet or a deer antler; because the tongues differ in length or thickness they produce two notes, usually about a third or a fourth apart. To begin, practise a four-syllable rhythm pattern: to and ko are the low note, ti and ki the high note; to and ti are the strong beats, ko and ki the weak, and then accompany dance or poetry recitation together with a skin drum.
特波那茲特鼓的實際聆聽場合，主要見於墨西哥中部阿茲特克及相關文化的舞蹈、詩歌朗誦: The actual listening contexts of the teponaztli are mainly dance, poetry recitation, celebration and war communication among the Aztecs and related cultures of central Mexico. It often plays together with the huehuetl skin drum, providing rhythm for various dances; in poetry recitation the drum strokes are also embedded in the text as syllable marks, which shows that it served as rhythmic accompaniment and a cue for speech. The source gives no specific composers or pieces, so the demonstration should centre on these contexts and ensemble line-ups.
特波那茲特鼓起源於中墨西哥的阿茲特克文明，是古代中美洲最重要的打擊樂器之一。這種: The teponaztli originates in the Aztec civilisation of central Mexico and is one of the most important percussion instruments of ancient Mesoamerica. This slit drum is hollowed from a single piece of wood, usually a hardwood, and has a distinctive resonance.
西班牙殖民後，特波那茲特鼓逐漸傳入其他中美洲地區和拉丁美洲。雖然使用範圍縮小，但: After the Spanish conquest the teponaztli gradually spread to other parts of Mesoamerica and Latin America. Although its range of use shrank, it has kept its vitality in the traditional music of Mexico and Central America. Today the teponaztli is an important object for the study of the musical heritage of pre-Columbian civilisations, and a symbol of the richness of ancient American cultures.
